name: Grammar in Context 2
description: Curso completo de gramática de nivel intermedio (14 unidades + apéndices), con tarjetas de regla y ejercicios de completar por sección.

decks.name: U1 · Presente simple y palabras de frecuencia
decks.description: Unidad 1 (Animals): el verbo be, el presente simple (forma, uso, negativos, preguntas) y las palabras de frecuencia.

cards.front: 1.1 · ¿Cuáles son las formas del verbo be en presente?
cards.back: Be tiene tres formas en presente: am (con I), is (con he/she/it y sustantivos singulares) y are (con you/we/they y plurales). Es el único verbo que cambia así según el sujeto.
cards.example: I am a student. / She is from Guatemala. / They are engineers. / The dog is friendly.
cards.audio: I am a student. / She is from Guatemala. / They are engineers. / The dog is friendly.

cards.front: 1.2 · ¿Cómo se forman las contracciones con be?
cards.back: En el habla y la escritura informal, el sujeto y be se unen con apóstrofo: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're. También se contraen con sustantivos (Denil's here) y con there/here/that (there's, that's). No se contrae am en respuestas cortas afirmativas: 'Yes, I am' (no 'Yes, I'm').
cards.example: I'm a programmer. / She's my sister. / They're at home. / That's a good idea.
cards.audio: I'm a programmer. / She's my sister. / They're at home. / That's a good idea.

cards.front: {{She's}} my best friend. (contracción de she is)
{{They're}} very busy today. (contracción de they are)
1.3 · ¿Para qué se usa el verbo be?
cards.back: Be sirve para: describir (adjetivos), clasificar (sustantivos), decir el origen o la ubicación, la edad, la hora, el clima, y con there is/are para decir que algo existe. En español a veces usamos 'tener' donde el inglés usa be: I am 25 years old, I am hungry/cold/thirsty.
cards.example: She is tall. / He is a teacher. / We are in class. / I am 22 years old. / It is cold today. / There is a cat on the roof.
cards.audio: She is tall. / He is a teacher. / We are in class. / I am 22 years old. / It is cold today. / There is a cat on the roof.

cards.back: Con hambre, sed, frío, edad… el inglés usa be, no have.
La edad se dice con be + número + years old.
Se pone not después de be: am not, is not, are not. Contracciones: isn't, aren't; también 's not / 're not (he's not, they're not). 'am not' no tiene contracción con not (I'm not).
cards.example: I'm not tired. / She isn't here. / They aren't ready. / He's not a lawyer.
cards.audio: I'm not tired. / She isn't here. / They aren't ready. / He's not a lawyer.

cards.front: The store {{isn't|is not}} open on Sundays.
I {{'m not|am not}} from the capital.
cards.back: I am not → I'm not (no existe 'amn't').

cards.front: 1.5 · ¿Cómo se hacen preguntas de sí/no con be y cómo se responden?
cards.back: Se invierte el orden: Be + sujeto + resto. Am I…? Is she…? Are they…? Las respuestas cortas repiten el sujeto y be: Yes, she is. / No, she isn't. En la respuesta afirmativa no se usa contracción.
cards.example: Are you a student? Yes, I am. / Is he at work? No, he isn't. / Are they from Mexico? Yes, they are.
cards.audio: Are you a student? Yes, I am. / Is he at work? No, he isn't. / Are they from Mexico? Yes, they are.

cards.front: {{Is}} your sister at home? — Yes, she {{is}}.
cards.back: Be va antes del sujeto en la pregunta; en la respuesta corta afirmativa no se contrae.

cards.front: 1.6 · ¿Cómo se forman las preguntas con palabra interrogativa (wh-) y be?
cards.back: Palabra wh- + be + sujeto: Where is she? What are they? How old is he? Why are you late? Las palabras: what, where, when, why, who, how, how old, how much, what time, what kind of. Con who como sujeto no hay inversión: Who is your teacher?
cards.example: Where are you from? / What time is it? / How old is your brother? / Why is the door open? / Who is that man?
cards.audio: Where are you from? / What time is it? / How old is your brother? / Why is the door open? / Who is that man?

cards.front: {{Where}} are you from? — I'm from Sacatepéquez.

cards.back: What time + is it para la hora.

cards.front: 1.7 · ¿Cómo se forma el presente simple afirmativo?
cards.back: Con I/you/we/they se usa la forma base del verbo. Con he/she/it se añade -s (o -es después de sh, ch, ss, x, o; y tras consonante → -ies). Excepciones: have → has, go → goes, do → does.
cards.example: I work in the city. / She works at a bank. / He watches TV. / My cat studies me. / She has two jobs.
cards.audio: I work in the city. / She works at a bank. / He watches TV. / My cat studies me. / She has two jobs.

cards.back: Para hechos y verdades generales, hábitos y rutinas, costumbres, y con verbos de estado (like, want, need, know). Suele ir con palabras de frecuencia (always, usually, every day).
cards.example: Water boils at 100 °C. / I drink coffee every morning. / Guatemalans eat tamales in December. / She likes jazz.
cards.audio: Water boils at 100 °C. / I drink coffee every morning. / Guatemalans eat tamales in December. / She likes jazz.

cards.front: 1.9 · ¿Cómo se forma el negativo del presente simple?
cards.back: Se usa don't (I/you/we/they) o doesn't (he/she/it) + verbo en forma base. Nunca se pone -s al verbo principal cuando hay doesn't.
cards.example: I don't eat meat. / She doesn't like coffee. / They don't work on Sundays. / It doesn't matter.
cards.audio: I don't eat meat. / She doesn't like coffee. / They don't work on Sundays. / It doesn't matter.

cards.back: Después de doesn't el verbo va sin -s.

cards.front: 1.10 · ¿Cómo se hacen preguntas en presente simple?
cards.back: Sí/no: Do/Does + sujeto + verbo base. Wh-: palabra wh- + do/does + sujeto + verbo base. Respuestas cortas: Yes, I do. / No, she doesn't. Con who/what como sujeto no se usa do: Who lives here?
cards.example: Do you like pizza? / Does she work here? / Where do they live? / What does he do? / Who knows the answer?
cards.audio: Do you like pizza? / Does she work here? / Where do they live? / What does he do? / Who knows the answer?

cards.front: What {{does}} she do? — She's a nurse.
cards.back: 'What does she do?' pregunta por la profesión.

cards.front: 1.11 · ¿Dónde va la preposición en una pregunta wh-?
cards.back: En inglés conversacional la preposición va al final de la pregunta: Where are you from? Who do you live with? What is she interested in? En estilo muy formal puede ir al inicio (With whom…?), pero es raro.
cards.example: Where are you from? / Who do you work with? / What are you thinking about? / What is this made of?
cards.audio: Where are you from? / Who do you work with? / What are you thinking about? / What is this made of?

cards.back: En preguntas wh- la preposición suele ir al final.

cards.front: 1.12 · ¿Cómo se pregunta por el significado, la ortografía, el costo y la hora?
cards.back: What does 'X' mean? (significado) / How do you spell 'X'? (ortografía) / How do you say 'X' in English? (traducción) / How much does it cost? (costo) / What time is it? (hora). Se usan do/does porque mean, spell, say y cost son verbos normales.
cards.example: What does 'deadline' mean? / How do you spell your last name? / How do you say 'chucho' in English? / How much does the ticket cost?
cards.audio: What does 'deadline' mean? / How do you spell your last name? / How do you say 'chucho' in English? / How much does the ticket cost?

cards.back: cost es verbo: does it cost.

cards.front: 1.13 · ¿Cuáles son las palabras de frecuencia y qué significan?
cards.back: De más a menos: always (100 %), usually/generally, often/frequently, sometimes, rarely/seldom, hardly ever, never (0 %). Se usan con el presente simple para decir con qué frecuencia ocurre algo.
cards.example: I always brush my teeth. / She usually takes the bus. / We sometimes eat out. / He never smokes.
cards.audio: I always brush my teeth. / She usually takes the bus. / We sometimes eat out. / He never smokes.

cards.front: 1.14 · ¿Dónde se colocan las palabras de frecuencia en la oración?
cards.back: Van después del verbo be (She is always late) pero antes de los demás verbos (She always comes late). Sometimes, usually y often también pueden ir al inicio de la oración. Con negativo: She isn't usually late / She doesn't usually come late.
cards.example: He is never home. / He never stays home. / Sometimes I cook. / I don't often travel.
cards.audio: He is never home. / He never stays home. / Sometimes I cook. / I don't often travel.

cards.front: He {{is always}} late for class. (be + always)
He {{always comes}} late to class. (always + come)
1.15 · ¿Cómo se hacen preguntas con palabras de frecuencia?
cards.back: En preguntas sí/no la palabra de frecuencia va después del sujeto: Do you ever eat sushi? Is she always this happy? 'Ever' se usa en preguntas y significa 'alguna vez'.
cards.example: Do you ever go to the beach? / Is he usually this quiet? / Does she always work on Saturdays?
cards.audio: Do you ever go to the beach? / Is he usually this quiet? / Does she always work on Saturdays?

cards.front: Are you {{always}} this tired on Mondays?
1.16 · ¿Cómo se pregunta por la frecuencia con how often?
cards.back: How often + do/does + sujeto + verbo. Se responde con expresiones como once a day, twice a week, three times a month, every day, every other day.
cards.example: How often do you exercise? — Twice a week. / How often does she call? — Every day.
cards.audio: How often do you exercise? — Twice a week. / How often does she call? — Every day.

cards.front: How {{often}} do you go to the gym? — Three times a week.
I visit my grandparents {{twice}} a month. (2 veces)

decks.name: U2 · Presente continuo y futuro
decks.description: Unidad 2 (Across Generations): el presente continuo, presente simple vs. continuo, verbos de acción y de estado, y el futuro con will, be going to y presente continuo.

cards.back: Sujeto + am/is/are + verbo-ing. Ortografía del -ing: verbos en -e pierden la e (make → making); consonante-vocal-consonante duplica la última (run → running, sit → sitting); -ie → -ying (lie → lying).
cards.example: I am studying now. / She is making dinner. / They are running in the park. / He is lying on the sofa.
cards.audio: I am studying now. / She is making dinner. / They are running in the park. / He is lying on the sofa.

cards.front: She {{is watching}} a movie right now.
They are {{running}} to catch the bus.

cards.back: Para acciones que ocurren en este momento (now, right now, at the moment), para acciones en progreso en un periodo actual aunque no ocurran ahora mismo (this semester, these days), y para situaciones temporales o tendencias (More people are working from home).
cards.example: I'm reading a great book these days. / She's studying at UVG this year. / Prices are rising.
cards.audio: I'm reading a great book these days. / She's studying at UVG this year. / Prices are rising.

cards.front: This semester I {{am taking}} six courses.
cards.back: Periodo actual aunque no sea ahora mismo.

cards.front: 2.3 · ¿Cómo se hacen preguntas con el presente continuo?
cards.back: Sí/no: Am/Is/Are + sujeto + verbo-ing. Wh-: palabra wh- + be + sujeto + verbo-ing. Respuestas cortas con be: Yes, I am. / No, he isn't.
cards.example: Are you listening? / Is she working today? / What are you doing? / Why is he crying?
cards.audio: Are you listening? / Is she working today? / What are you doing? / Why is he crying?

cards.front: 2.4 · ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre el presente simple y el presente continuo?
cards.back: Presente simple: hábitos, hechos y rutinas (every day, always). Presente continuo: acciones en progreso ahora o en el periodo actual (now, this week). Compara: I work at BYTE (hecho) vs. I'm working on a new feature (ahora).
cards.example: She usually drives to work, but today she is taking the bus. / He speaks three languages. / He is speaking with the manager right now.
cards.audio: She usually drives to work, but today she is taking the bus. / He speaks three languages. / He is speaking with the manager right now.

cards.front: I usually {{drink}} coffee, but today I {{am drinking}} tea.
Look! It {{is raining}}. It {{rains}} a lot in September.
2.5 · ¿Qué son los verbos de acción y de estado (nonaction)?
cards.back: Los verbos de estado describen estados, sentidos, emociones, posesión o pensamiento (know, like, want, need, believe, have, see, hear, own, cost) y normalmente NO se usan en continuo. Algunos cambian de significado: have (poseer, estado) vs. having lunch (acción); think (opinar) vs. thinking about (proceso); look (parecer) vs. looking at (acción).
cards.example: I know the answer. (no 'am knowing') / She has a car. / She is having lunch. / I think it's a good idea. / I'm thinking about my project.
cards.audio: I know the answer. (no 'am knowing') / She has a car. / She is having lunch. / I think it's a good idea. / I'm thinking about my project.

cards.back: want no se usa en continuo.

cards.front: We {{are having}} dinner right now. Call later.
2.6 · ¿Cómo se usa el futuro con will?
cards.back: Will + verbo base para todos los sujetos. Negativo: won't. Se usa para predicciones, promesas, ofrecimientos y decisiones tomadas en el momento de hablar. Contracción: I'll, you'll, she'll…
cards.example: It will be sunny tomorrow. / I'll help you with that. / Don't worry, I won't forget. / The phone is ringing. I'll get it!
cards.audio: It will be sunny tomorrow. / I'll help you with that. / Don't worry, I won't forget. / The phone is ringing. I'll get it!

cards.front: I promise I {{will|'ll}} call you tonight.

cards.back: Después de will el verbo va en forma base.

cards.front: 2.7 · ¿Cómo se usa el futuro con be going to?
cards.back: Am/is/are + going to + verbo base. Se usa para planes e intenciones ya decididos, y para predicciones basadas en evidencia presente (Look at those clouds. It's going to rain). En el habla informal suena 'gonna'.
cards.example: I'm going to study abroad next year. / They're going to buy a house. / Careful! You're going to fall.
cards.audio: I'm going to study abroad next year. / They're going to buy a house. / Careful! You're going to fall.

cards.front: We {{are going to}} visit Tikal in December. (plan)
Look at the sky. It {{is going to}} rain.
2.8 · ¿Cuándo se elige will, be going to o presente continuo para el futuro?
cards.back: Will: predicciones sin evidencia, promesas, ofrecimientos, decisiones espontáneas. Be going to: planes/intenciones y predicciones con evidencia. Presente continuo: planes fijos ya organizados con fecha, lugar o personas (I'm meeting Ana at 5). Con predicciones generales, will y be going to suelen ser intercambiables.
cards.example: I think she'll win. / I'm going to learn Kotlin this year. / We're having dinner with my parents on Sunday.
cards.audio: I think she'll win. / I'm going to learn Kotlin this year. / We're having dinner with my parents on Sunday.

cards.front: A: The phone is ringing. B: I {{'ll|will}} answer it. (decisión espontánea)
I {{am meeting}} the client at 10 tomorrow. It's in my calendar. (meet)
cards.back: Plan fijo con hora → presente continuo.

cards.front: 2.9 · ¿Qué tiempo verbal se usa en la cláusula de tiempo o de if con futuro?
cards.back: En la cláusula que empieza con when, before, after, until, as soon as o if se usa el PRESENTE simple, no will; el futuro va en la cláusula principal. Si la cláusula de tiempo va primero, se separa con coma.
cards.example: When I finish college, I'll work in aerospace. / I'll call you as soon as I arrive. / If it rains, we won't go.
cards.audio: When I finish college, I'll work in aerospace. / I'll call you as soon as I arrive. / If it rains, we won't go.

cards.front: When she {{arrives}}, we will start the meeting. (arrive)
cards.back: Tras when se usa presente, no will.

cards.front: If you {{study}}, you {{will|'ll}} pass the exam. (study / pass)
I'll send the report before I {{leave}} the office. (leave)

decks.name: U3 · Pasado simple y used to
decks.description: Unidad 3 (What Is Success?): el pasado simple (be, regulares, irregulares, negativos y preguntas) y el pasado habitual con used to.

cards.back: Verbos regulares: base + -ed (worked, played). Irregulares: forma propia (went, ate, saw). La forma es la misma para todos los sujetos. Be es la excepción: was (I/he/she/it) y were (you/we/they).
cards.example: I worked late yesterday. / She went to Xela last week. / They were tired. / He was at home.
cards.audio: I worked late yesterday. / She went to Xela last week. / They were tired. / He was at home.

cards.front: We {{went}} to the beach last summer. (go)

cards.back: Para acciones o estados terminados en un momento definido del pasado (yesterday, last week, in 2020, two days ago, when I was a child). Puede ser una sola acción, una serie de acciones o un hábito pasado.
cards.example: I graduated from Kinal in 2022. / She called me an hour ago. / When I was a kid, I played soccer every day.
cards.audio: I graduated from Kinal in 2022. / She called me an hour ago. / When I was a kid, I played soccer every day.

cards.front: She {{moved}} to the capital two years {{ago}}. (move / hace)
cards.back: 'ago' va después del periodo de tiempo.

cards.front: 3.3 · ¿Cómo se usa el pasado de be?
cards.back: Was con I/he/she/it; were con you/we/they. Negativo: wasn't/weren't. Preguntas: Was she…? Were they…? Where were you? También there was/there were.
cards.example: I was sick yesterday. / They were at the party. / Was he late? / There were many people.
cards.audio: I was sick yesterday. / They were at the party. / Was he late? / There were many people.

cards.front: Where {{were}} you last night? — I {{was}} at home.
cards.back: were con you; was con I.

cards.front: 3.4 · ¿Cómo se escriben y pronuncian los verbos regulares en pasado?
cards.back: Se añade -ed: verbo en -e solo añade -d (lived); consonante + y → -ied (studied); vocal + y → -yed (played); consonante-vocal-consonante acentuada duplica (stopped, planned). Pronunciación: /t/ tras sonido sordo (worked), /d/ tras sonoro (played), /ɪd/ tras t o d (wanted, needed).
cards.example: lived, studied, played, stopped, wanted / She stopped smoking. / We needed help.
cards.audio: lived, studied, played, stopped, wanted / She stopped smoking. / We needed help.

cards.front: 3.5 · ¿Cuáles son los verbos irregulares más comunes en pasado?
cards.back: No siguen la regla -ed y hay que memorizarlos. Algunos: go → went, have → had, do → did, see → saw, get → got, make → made, take → took, come → came, give → gave, know → knew, think → thought, buy → bought, eat → ate, write → wrote, read → read (pronunciado 'red'). Hay un mazo de apéndice con la lista completa.
cards.example: I had breakfast at 7. / She saw the movie. / We took a taxi. / He bought a new phone.
cards.audio: I had breakfast at 7. / She saw the movie. / We took a taxi. / He bought a new phone.

cards.front: 3.6 · ¿Cómo se forman los negativos y las preguntas en pasado simple?
cards.back: Negativo: didn't + verbo base (para todos los sujetos). Preguntas: Did + sujeto + verbo base; wh-: Where did you go? Respuestas cortas: Yes, I did. / No, she didn't. Con who/what como sujeto no se usa did: Who called?
cards.example: I didn't see him. / Did you finish? / What did she say? / Who won the game?
cards.audio: I didn't see him. / Did you finish? / What did she say? / Who won the game?

cards.front: We {{didn't|did not}} go to class yesterday.

cards.back: Tras did el verbo va en forma base.

cards.front: 3.7 · ¿Cómo se usa used to para el pasado habitual?
cards.back: Used to + verbo base describe hábitos o situaciones del pasado que ya no ocurren. Negativo: didn't use to (sin -d). Pregunta: Did you use to…? No se usa para una sola acción pasada ni con expresiones de duración exacta.
cards.example: I used to live in Ciudad Vieja. / She used to smoke, but she quit. / Did you use to play chess? / He didn't use to like vegetables.
cards.audio: I used to live in Ciudad Vieja. / She used to smoke, but she quit. / Did you use to play chess? / He didn't use to like vegetables.

cards.front: I {{used to}} play the piano when I was a child, but I don't anymore.
She didn't {{use}} to like coffee. (tras didn't)
cards.back: Tras didn't se escribe use to, sin -d.

cards.front: {{Did}} your family use to live in Antigua?

decks.name: U4 · Posesivos y pronombres
decks.description: Unidad 4 (Weddings): formas posesivas, pronombres de objeto y reflexivos, objeto directo e indirecto, say y tell, preguntas de sujeto y wh-.

cards.front: 4.1 · ¿Cuáles son las formas posesivas y los pronombres personales?
cards.back: Sujeto: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Objeto: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. Adjetivo posesivo: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. Pronombre posesivo: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Reflexivo: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves.
cards.example: I / me / my / mine / myself. / She loves him. / This is her book. / The book is hers.
cards.audio: I / me / my / mine / myself. / She loves him. / This is her book. / The book is hers.

cards.front: 4.2 · ¿Cómo se forma el posesivo de los sustantivos?
cards.back: Singular: 's (my sister's car). Plural en -s: solo apóstrofo (my parents' house). Plural irregular: 's (children's toys). Nombres propios en -s: 's o solo ' (Carlos's / Carlos'). Con objetos inanimados se prefiere of: the door of the car.
cards.example: Denil's laptop / the students' projects / the women's team / the end of the movie
cards.audio: Denil's laptop / the students' projects / the women's team / the end of the movie

cards.front: My {{brother's}} car is red. (brother, un hermano)
My {{parents'}} house is in Ciudad Vieja. (parents, plural)
cards.back: Solo apóstrofo tras la s del plural.

My, your, his, her, its, our, their van siempre antes de un sustantivo y concuerdan con el poseedor, no con la cosa poseída (his sister, her brother). Ojo: its (posesivo) ≠ it's (it is); their ≠ they're ≠ there.
cards.example: She loves her job. / He visits his parents. / The dog wags its tail. / They sold their house.
cards.audio: She loves her job. / He visits his parents. / The dog wags its tail. / They sold their house.

cards.front: Ana talks to {{her}} mother every day. (Ana, poseedor femenino)
The company changed {{its}} logo. (posesivo de it)

cards.back: Mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs sustituyen a adjetivo posesivo + sustantivo para no repetirlo: Your car is new; mine is old. Nunca llevan sustantivo después ni apóstrofo. Whose pregunta por el dueño: Whose is this? It's hers.
cards.example: This phone is mine. / Their house is bigger than ours. / Is this book yours?
cards.audio: This phone is mine. / Their house is bigger than ours. / Is this book yours?

cards.front: That jacket isn't mine. It's {{hers}}. (de ella)
Our project is done. Is {{yours}} finished too?

cards.back: Whose + sustantivo + be/verbo auxiliar + sujeto: Whose phone is this? Whose keys are these? Whose car did you take? También puede ir solo: Whose is this? No confundir con who's (who is).
cards.example: Whose backpack is this? — It's Marta's. / Whose idea was it?
cards.audio: Whose backpack is this? — It's Marta's. / Whose idea was it?

cards.back: who's = who is; whose = de quién.

cards.front: 4.6 · ¿Cómo se usan los pronombres de objeto?
cards.back: Me, you, him, her, it, us, them van después de un verbo (I saw him) o de una preposición (with her, for us, about them). Nunca se usa el pronombre de sujeto en esas posiciones.
cards.example: She called me yesterday. / We'll go with them. / This gift is for you. / Don't tell him.
cards.audio: She called me yesterday. / We'll go with them. / This gift is for you. / Don't tell him.

cards.front: Do you know Luis? — Yes, I know {{him}} well.

cards.back: Cuando el sujeto y el objeto son la misma persona (She cut herself), para dar énfasis (I built it myself) y en expresiones: by myself (solo), enjoy yourself, help yourself, talk to yourself. Formas: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves.
cards.example: He hurt himself playing soccer. / We painted the house ourselves. / She lives by herself.
cards.audio: He hurt himself playing soccer. / We painted the house ourselves. / She lives by herself.

cards.front: I looked at {{myself}} in the mirror.
They built the app {{themselves}}. (énfasis: ellos mismos)
4.8 · ¿Cómo se ordenan el objeto directo y el indirecto?
cards.back: Dos órdenes: verbo + objeto directo + to/for + objeto indirecto (She gave the book to me) o verbo + objeto indirecto + objeto directo (She gave me the book). Si el objeto directo es un pronombre (it/them), va primero: She gave it to me (no 'gave me it'). To: give, send, show, tell, lend, hand. For: buy, make, get, cook, find.
cards.example: I sent an email to my boss. / I sent my boss an email. / He bought a gift for her. / He bought her a gift.
cards.audio: I sent an email to my boss. / I sent my boss an email. / He bought a gift for her. / He bought her a gift.

cards.front: She gave {{me}} the keys. (a mí, sin preposición)
I made a cake {{for}} my mother.
4.9 · ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre say y tell?
cards.back: Tell lleva objeto de persona directamente: tell me, tell him the truth. Say no lleva objeto de persona directo; si se menciona, se usa to: say hello to her. Expresiones: tell a story/the truth/a lie/a joke; say yes/no/hello/goodbye.
cards.example: He told me the news. / He said the news was bad. / Say hello to your parents. / Don't tell lies.
cards.audio: He told me the news. / He said the news was bad. / Say hello to your parents. / Don't tell lies.

cards.front: She {{told}} me about the wedding. (say/tell, pasado)

cards.back: Cuando who, what, which o how many preguntan por el sujeto, NO se usa do/does/did y el verbo va en tercera persona singular: Who lives here? What happened? Which team won? How many people came?
cards.example: Who wants coffee? / What made that noise? / Who called you? (sujeto) vs. Who did you call? (objeto)
cards.audio: Who wants coffee? / What made that noise? / Who called you? (sujeto) vs. Who did you call? (objeto)

cards.front: Who {{lives}} in that house? (live; pregunta de sujeto)

cards.back: Pregunta de sujeto en pasado: sin did.

cards.front: 4.11 · ¿Cómo se forman las preguntas wh- en general?
cards.back: Palabra wh- + auxiliar (be/do/does/did/will) + sujeto + verbo. What (qué), which (cuál, de un grupo), who (quién), whom (a quién, formal), whose (de quién), where, when, why, how, how much/many/long/often.
cards.example: Which one do you prefer? / How long did the trip take? / Why didn't she come? / Where will you live?
cards.audio: Which one do you prefer? / How long did the trip take? / Why didn't she come? / Where will you live?

cards.front: {{Which}} dress do you like, the red one or the blue one?
How {{long}} did the ceremony last? — Two hours.
How {{many}} guests came to the wedding? — About 200.

decks.name: U5 · Sustantivos, there + be y cantidad
decks.description: Unidad 5 (American Heritage): plurales, contables e incontables, unidades de medida, there is/are, some/any/a/no, a few/few, a little/little, too much/many.

cards.front: 5.1 · ¿Cómo se forma el plural de los sustantivos?
cards.back: Regla general: + -s (books). Tras s, ss, sh, ch, x, z: + -es (boxes, dishes). Consonante + y → -ies (cities); vocal + y → -ys (days). Algunos en -o: + -es (tomatoes, potatoes, heroes) pero photos, pianos. -f/-fe → -ves (leaf → leaves, knife → knives). Irregulares: man → men, woman → women, child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, mouse → mice, person → people; iguales: fish, sheep, deer.
cards.example: two boxes / three cities / many potatoes / the leaves / five children / ten people
cards.audio: two boxes / three cities / many potatoes / the leaves / five children / ten people

cards.front: There are three {{children}} in the park. (child)
I need two {{boxes}} for the move. (box)
She brushes her {{teeth}} twice a day. (tooth)
5.2 · ¿Cómo se hacen generalizaciones con el plural?
cards.back: Para hablar de una categoría en general se usa el plural sin artículo (Dogs are loyal; Computers are useful). No se usa 'the' para generalizar: 'The dogs are loyal' se refiere a unos perros específicos.
cards.example: Cats sleep a lot. / Teachers work hard. / Programmers drink a lot of coffee.
cards.audio: Cats sleep a lot. / Teachers work hard. / Programmers drink a lot of coffee.

cards.front: I think {{engineers}} should learn to communicate well. (engineer, en general)
5.3 · ¿Qué casos especiales hay de singular y plural?
cards.back: Sustantivos siempre plurales: pants, jeans, glasses, scissors, clothes (a pair of jeans). Terminan en -s pero son singulares: news, mathematics, physics, economics, the United States. Police y people son plurales (The police are here). Family/team/class pueden ser singulares en inglés americano.
cards.example: These jeans are new. / The news is good. / The police are investigating. / Mathematics is my favorite subject.
cards.audio: These jeans are new. / The news is good. / The police are investigating. / Mathematics is my favorite subject.

cards.front: The police {{are}} looking for the thief. (be)
5.4 · ¿Qué son los sustantivos contables e incontables?
cards.back: Contables: tienen singular y plural y aceptan a/an y números (a book, two books). Incontables: no tienen plural ni llevan a/an; van con verbo singular y con some/much/a little (water, rice, money, furniture, information, advice, homework, music, bread, coffee, air).
cards.example: I need some information. / Furniture is expensive. / She gave me good advice. / Can I have a glass of water?
cards.audio: I need some information. / Furniture is expensive. / She gave me good advice. / Can I have a glass of water?

cards.front: I need {{some}} advice about my career. (a/some)
We have a lot of {{homework}} tonight. (homework/homeworks)
5.5 · ¿Qué sustantivos pueden ser contables e incontables con distinto significado?
cards.back: Algunos cambian de sentido: paper (papel, incontable) / a paper (un trabajo escrito, un periódico); chicken (carne) / a chicken (un animal); time (tiempo) / three times (veces); glass (vidrio) / a glass (un vaso); experience (experiencia general) / an experience (una vivencia); coffee (bebida) / two coffees (dos tazas, informal).
cards.example: I need paper. / I wrote a paper. / We ate chicken. / He has three chickens. / I don't have time. / I've been there two times.
cards.audio: I need paper. / I wrote a paper. / We ate chicken. / He has three chickens. / I don't have time. / I've been there two times.

cards.front: I don't have {{time}} to cook today. (tiempo, incontable)

cards.back: glass = vidrio; a glass = un vaso.

cards.front: 5.6 · ¿Cómo se cuentan los incontables con unidades de medida?
cards.back: Se usa una unidad + of + incontable: a cup of coffee, a glass of water, a bottle of milk, a piece of advice/information/furniture, a slice of bread, a bag of rice, a pound of meat, a gallon of gas, a bar of soap, a loaf of bread.
cards.example: two cups of coffee / a piece of information / three slices of pizza / a bottle of water
cards.audio: two cups of coffee / a piece of information / three slices of pizza / a bottle of water

cards.front: Can I have a {{glass}} of water?
She gave me a good {{piece}} of advice.
We need a {{loaf}} of bread for the sandwiches.
5.7 · ¿Cuándo se usa a lot of, much y many?
cards.back: A lot of / lots of: con contables e incontables, en afirmativas, negativas y preguntas. Many: con contables plurales. Much: con incontables, sobre todo en negativas y preguntas (no suena natural en afirmativas: 'I have much money' → 'a lot of money'). How many…? / How much…?
cards.example: I have a lot of friends. / She doesn't have much time. / How many books do you have? / How much money do you need?
cards.audio: I have a lot of friends. / She doesn't have much time. / How many books do you have? / How much money do you need?

cards.front: How {{much}} water do you drink a day?
I don't have {{much}} experience with iOS.

cards.back: There is + singular/incontable; there are + plural. Sirve para decir que algo existe o está en un lugar. Negativo: there isn't / there aren't (o there's no / there are no). Preguntas: Is there…? Are there…? Pasado: there was / there were. Futuro: there will be.
cards.example: There is a park near my house. / There are two banks on this street. / Is there any milk? / There was a storm last night.
cards.audio: There is a park near my house. / There are two banks on this street. / Is there any milk? / There was a storm last night.

cards.front: There {{is}} a lot of traffic in the city today. (be)
5.9 · ¿Cuándo se usa some, any, a y no?
cards.back: A/an: contable singular. Some: afirmativas (con plural o incontable) y ofrecimientos/peticiones (Would you like some coffee?). Any: negativas y preguntas (I don't have any money; Do you have any questions?). No: con verbo afirmativo = 'ningún' (There is no milk = There isn't any milk).
cards.example: I bought some apples. / We don't have any eggs. / Do you have any brothers? / There's no time.
cards.audio: I bought some apples. / We don't have any eggs. / Do you have any brothers? / There's no time.

cards.front: I don't have {{any}} cash on me.
There are {{some}} cookies in the kitchen. (afirmativa)
There is {{no}} milk left. (verbo afirmativo, 'nada de')
cards.back: there is no = there isn't any.

cards.front: 5.10 · ¿Cómo se usan a few, several y a little?
cards.back: A few y several: con contables plurales (a few friends, several problems). A little: con incontables (a little sugar, a little time). Los tres significan una cantidad pequeña pero suficiente.
cards.example: I have a few questions. / We visited several countries. / Add a little salt.
cards.audio: I have a few questions. / We visited several countries. / Add a little salt.

cards.front: Could you add a {{little}} milk to my coffee? (incontable)
5.11 · ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre a few / few y a little / little?
cards.back: Con 'a' el sentido es positivo (algunos, suficientes): I have a few friends here. Sin 'a' el sentido es negativo (casi ninguno, no suficientes): I have few friends here (me siento solo). Igual con a little (algo) vs. little (casi nada): There is little hope.
cards.example: She has a little money, so she can eat out. / She has little money, so she can't go out. / Few students passed the exam.
cards.audio: She has a little money, so she can eat out. / She has little money, so she can't go out. / Few students passed the exam.

cards.front: He has {{few}} friends, so he feels lonely. (casi ninguno)
He has {{a few}} friends, so he's happy. (algunos)
There is {{little}} time left; hurry up! (casi nada)
5.12 · ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre too much / too many y a lot of?
cards.back: A lot of es neutro: mucha cantidad. Too much (incontable) y too many (contable) indican exceso, más de lo deseable, con matiz negativo: I ate too much cake (me sentí mal). 'Too' no significa 'muy'.
cards.example: She has a lot of energy. (bien) / She drinks too much coffee. (problema) / There are too many cars downtown.
cards.audio: She has a lot of energy. (bien) / She drinks too much coffee. (problema) / There are too many cars downtown.

cards.front: I have {{a lot of}} homework, but it's fine. (mucha, sin problema)
There are {{too many}} people in this room; I can't breathe. (contable, exceso)
Don't put {{too much}} salt in the soup. (incontable, exceso)

decks.name: U6 · Adjetivos, modificadores y adverbios
decks.description: Unidad 6 (A Healthy Planet, a Healthy Body): adjetivos, sustantivos modificadores, adverbios, adjetivos vs. adverbios, too/too much/too many/enough, too vs. very.

cards.back: Un sustantivo puede modificarse con un adjetivo (a big house), con otro sustantivo (a coffee cup) o con ambos; el modificador va siempre ANTES del sustantivo y no cambia a plural: two big houses, three coffee cups.
cards.example: a healthy diet / a science teacher / an expensive Italian car
cards.audio: a healthy diet / a science teacher / an expensive Italian car

cards.back: El adjetivo va antes y no tiene plural.

cards.front: I need a {{coffee}} cup. (sustantivo que modifica)

cards.back: Van antes del sustantivo o después de be/seem/look/feel (She is happy; It looks great). No tienen plural. Muchos terminan en -ed (bored, tired = cómo se siente alguien) o -ing (boring, tiring = cómo es algo). Adjetivos de nacionalidad y colores también son adjetivos.
cards.example: The movie was boring, so I was bored. / He seems tired. / a Guatemalan restaurant
cards.audio: The movie was boring, so I was bored. / He seems tired. / a Guatemalan restaurant

cards.front: The lecture was {{boring}}, so the students were {{bored}}. (-ing / -ed)
6.3 · ¿Cómo se usan los sustantivos como modificadores?
cards.back: Un sustantivo puede describir a otro y va antes, siempre en singular: a shoe store (no 'shoes store'), a ten-minute walk, a two-year-old child. Con números se une con guion y el sustantivo queda singular.
cards.example: a bus stop / a history teacher / a three-hour flight / a five-dollar bill
cards.audio: a bus stop / a history teacher / a three-hour flight / a five-dollar bill

cards.front: It's a {{ten-minute}} walk to the station. (ten minutes → modificador)
cards.back: Como modificador, minute va en singular con guion.

cards.front: I bought it at a {{shoe}} store. (shoe/shoes)
6.4 · ¿Cómo se forman y usan los adverbios de modo?
cards.back: Describen cómo se hace una acción y suelen formarse con adjetivo + -ly (quick → quickly, careful → carefully; -y → -ily: easy → easily; -le → -ly: simple → simply). Van después del verbo o del objeto (She speaks English fluently). Irregulares: good → well, fast → fast, hard → hard, late → late, early → early.
cards.example: He drives carefully. / She sings beautifully. / They work hard. / I speak Spanish well.
cards.audio: He drives carefully. / She sings beautifully. / They work hard. / I speak Spanish well.

cards.front: 6.5 · ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre adjetivo y adverbio?
cards.back: El adjetivo describe un sustantivo (a careful driver; she is careful) y el adverbio describe un verbo (she drives carefully). Tras verbos de sentido o estado (look, seem, feel, sound, taste, smell, be) se usa ADJETIVO: The soup tastes good; She looks tired.
cards.example: He is a quick learner. / He learns quickly. / You look great today. / This music sounds nice.
cards.audio: He is a quick learner. / He learns quickly. / You look great today. / This music sounds nice.

cards.front: She did the exam {{quickly}} and left. (quick/quickly)
6.6 · ¿Cómo se usan too, too much, too many y enough?
cards.back: Too + adjetivo/adverbio (too hot, too fast); too much + incontable; too many + contable: exceso, problema. Enough va DESPUÉS del adjetivo/adverbio (big enough, fast enough) y ANTES del sustantivo (enough money). Often + to + verbo: too tired to study; old enough to vote.
cards.example: The coffee is too hot to drink. / I have too much work. / There aren't enough chairs. / He isn't tall enough to reach it.
cards.audio: The coffee is too hot to drink. / I have too much work. / There aren't enough chairs. / He isn't tall enough to reach it.

cards.front: This room isn't big {{enough}} for 20 people. (posición)
We don't have {{enough}} time to finish. (posición)
I'm {{too}} tired to go out tonight. (exceso)
6.7 · ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre too y very?
cards.back: Very intensifica sin juicio negativo (very tall = muy alto). Too implica exceso y un problema (too tall to fit = demasiado alto para caber). En español 'demasiado' a veces se usa como 'muy', pero en inglés too siempre suena a problema.
cards.example: The soup is very hot, but I like it. / The soup is too hot; I can't eat it. / She is very smart.
cards.audio: The soup is very hot, but I like it. / The soup is too hot; I can't eat it. / She is very smart.

cards.front: This coat is {{very}} warm; I love it. (sin problema)
This coat is {{too}} small; it doesn't fit me. (problema)

decks.name: U7 · Palabras de tiempo y pasado continuo
decks.description: Unidad 7 (A New Start): time words (for, during, in, ago…), when/whenever, el pasado continuo y su contraste con el pasado simple, y -ing tras palabras de tiempo.

cards.front: 7.1 · ¿Cómo se usan las palabras de tiempo (in, on, at, for, during, ago, until, by)?
cards.back: In + mes/año/estación (in 2020, in July) y in + periodo = dentro de (in two weeks). On + día/fecha (on Monday, on May 5). At + hora (at 7). For + duración (for three years). During + evento/periodo (during the class). Ago = hace (two days ago). Until = hasta que termina (until 5). By = a más tardar (by Friday). From… to… (from 9 to 5). While + cláusula; during + sustantivo.
cards.example: I moved here in 2023. / The meeting is on Friday at 3. / We talked for an hour. / She fell asleep during the movie. / I'll finish by Monday.
cards.audio: I moved here in 2023. / The meeting is on Friday at 3. / We talked for an hour. / She fell asleep during the movie. / I'll finish by Monday.

cards.front: We lived in Xela {{for}} five years. (duración)
My grandparents came to the city 40 years {{ago}}. (hace)
The report is due {{by}} Friday. (a más tardar)
7.2 · ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre when y whenever?
cards.back: When = cuando (un momento o cada vez, en contexto). Whenever = cada vez que, siempre que (énfasis en repetición o en 'no importa cuándo'). Ambos introducen una cláusula de tiempo.
cards.example: When I arrived, she was cooking. / Whenever I visit Antigua, I eat at the same place. / Call me whenever you need help.
cards.audio: When I arrived, she was cooking. / Whenever I visit Antigua, I eat at the same place. / Call me whenever you need help.

cards.front: {{Whenever}} I feel stressed, I go for a walk. (cada vez que)
{{When}} did you move to the city? (en qué momento)

cards.back: Was/were + verbo-ing. Was con I/he/she/it, were con you/we/they. Negativo: wasn't/weren't + -ing. Preguntas: Was she working? What were you doing?
cards.example: I was studying at 10 p.m. / They were playing soccer. / She wasn't listening. / Were you sleeping?
cards.audio: I was studying at 10 p.m. / They were playing soccer. / She wasn't listening. / Were you sleeping?

cards.front: At 8 p.m. last night, I {{was watching}} a movie. (watch)
7.4 · ¿Cómo se usa el pasado continuo con una hora específica?
cards.back: Describe una acción que estaba en progreso en un momento concreto del pasado: At 9 o'clock I was driving to work. La acción empezó antes y continuó después de esa hora.
cards.example: At midnight, we were still dancing. / This time last year, I was living in Antigua.
cards.audio: At midnight, we were still dancing. / This time last year, I was living in Antigua.

cards.front: At 7 a.m. yesterday, I {{was eating}} breakfast. (eat)
7.5 · ¿Cómo se usa el pasado continuo con una cláusula de when?
cards.back: La acción larga en progreso va en pasado continuo y la acción corta que la interrumpe va en pasado simple con when: I was sleeping when the phone rang. También: When the phone rang, I was sleeping.
cards.example: She was cooking when the lights went out. / When I saw him, he was crossing the street.
cards.audio: She was cooking when the lights went out. / When I saw him, he was crossing the street.

cards.front: I {{was taking}} a shower when the phone {{rang}}. (take / ring)
When we {{arrived}}, they {{were having}} dinner. (arrive / have)
7.6 · ¿Cómo se usa el pasado continuo con while?
cards.back: While introduce la acción en progreso: While I was studying, my roommate was cooking (dos acciones simultáneas en continuo). O: While I was studying, the lights went out (interrupción). While + cláusula con verbo; during + sustantivo.
cards.example: While she was driving, she was talking on the phone. / The baby woke up while we were eating.
cards.audio: While she was driving, she was talking on the phone. / The baby woke up while we were eating.

cards.front: {{While}} I was walking home, I saw an accident. (while/during)
While he {{was studying}}, his sister {{was playing}} video games. (study / play; simultáneas)
7.7 · ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre pasado simple y pasado continuo con when?
cards.back: When + pasado simple, pasado continuo → la acción larga ya estaba en progreso cuando ocurrió la corta: When I got home, she was cooking (ya cocinaba). When + pasado simple, pasado simple → una acción ocurre DESPUÉS de la otra: When I got home, she cooked (empezó a cocinar al llegar).
cards.example: When the teacher came in, the students were talking. (ya hablaban) / When the teacher came in, the students stopped talking. (después)
cards.audio: When the teacher came in, the students were talking. (ya hablaban) / When the teacher came in, the students stopped talking. (después)

cards.front: When I arrived, everyone {{was dancing}}. (dance; ya estaban bailando)
When I arrived, everyone {{stopped}} talking. (stop; reacción después)
7.8 · ¿Cómo se usa la forma -ing después de palabras de tiempo?
cards.back: Tras before, after, while, when y since se puede usar verbo-ing en vez de sujeto + verbo cuando el sujeto es el mismo: After eating, we left (= After we ate). Before leaving, check the door. También: since moving here.
cards.example: Before going to bed, I read. / After graduating, she got a job. / While waiting, I read the news.
cards.audio: Before going to bed, I read. / After graduating, she got a job. / While waiting, I read the news.

cards.front: After {{finishing}} the exam, we went out to celebrate. (finish)
Before {{leaving}} the house, turn off the lights. (leave)

decks.name: U8 · Modales
decks.description: Unidad 8 (Where We Live): modales y modales frasales: must/have to, may/be allowed to, be supposed to, can/could/be able to, should/ought to/had better, negativos, must (deducción), may/might, cortesía.

cards.back: Modales: can, could, should, will, would, may, might, must. Van siempre seguidos de la forma base del verbo (no de 'to'), no cambian según el sujeto (she can, no 'she cans'), forman el negativo con not y la pregunta invirtiendo con el sujeto: Can she swim? Should I go?
cards.example: He can code in Kotlin. / You should rest. / May I come in? / We must leave now.
cards.audio: He can code in Kotlin. / You should rest. / May I come in? / We must leave now.

cards.back: Los modales no cambian con he/she.

cards.front: You should {{see}} a doctor. (see; forma tras modal)

cards.back: Expresiones con significado modal que sí cambian según el sujeto y el tiempo: have to / has to / had to (obligación), be able to (habilidad), be allowed to / be permitted to (permiso), be supposed to (expectativa), ought to (consejo), had better (advertencia).
cards.example: She has to work on Saturdays. / We were able to fix it. / You're not allowed to park here.
cards.audio: She has to work on Saturdays. / We were able to fix it. / You're not allowed to park here.

cards.front: He {{has to}} wake up at 5 a.m. every day. (have to, he)
cards.back: have to sí cambia: has to.

cards.front: Last year I {{had to}} take the bus every day. (have to, pasado)
cards.back: must no tiene pasado; se usa had to.

cards.front: 8.3 · ¿Cómo se expresa obligación o necesidad con must y have to?
cards.back: Must: obligación fuerte, a menudo por regla o ley, o por convicción del hablante; más formal/escrito. Have to / have got to: necesidad u obligación en general, más usado al hablar. Pasado y futuro: had to, will have to (must no tiene esas formas).
cards.example: Drivers must stop at red lights. / I have to finish this tonight. / She had to cancel the trip. / You'll have to wait.
cards.audio: Drivers must stop at red lights. / I have to finish this tonight. / She had to cancel the trip. / You'll have to wait.

cards.front: All passengers {{must}} show their ID. (regla oficial)
I {{have to}} study tonight; I have an exam tomorrow. (necesidad personal, informal)
We will {{have to}} move next year. (obligación futura)
8.4 · ¿Cómo se expresa permiso y prohibición con may y los modales frasales?
cards.back: Permiso: may (formal), can (informal), be allowed to / be permitted to. Prohibición: may not, can't, be not allowed to, must not (mustn't = está prohibido). Ojo: don't have to = no es necesario (no es prohibición).
cards.example: Students may use dictionaries. / You can't smoke here. / Tenants aren't allowed to have pets. / You must not enter.
cards.audio: Students may use dictionaries. / You can't smoke here. / Tenants aren't allowed to have pets. / You must not enter.

cards.front: You {{are not allowed to|aren't allowed to}} park here. (be allowed to, negativo)
Visitors {{may}} not take photos inside the museum. (formal)

cards.back: Be supposed to + verbo base expresa lo que se espera por reglas, acuerdos o planes: I'm supposed to be at work at 8 (pero quizá no lo estoy). En pasado, was/were supposed to sugiere que no ocurrió: He was supposed to call me.
cards.example: You're supposed to wear a helmet. / We're supposed to meet at 6. / It was supposed to rain, but it didn't.
cards.audio: You're supposed to wear a helmet. / We're supposed to meet at 6. / It was supposed to rain, but it didn't.

cards.front: You {{are supposed to}} turn off your phone in class. (se espera que)
She {{was supposed to}} arrive at 9, but she's late. (pasado; no ocurrió)
8.6 · ¿Cómo se expresa habilidad y permiso con can, could y be able to?
cards.back: Can: habilidad presente y permiso informal. Could: habilidad en el pasado (I could swim at 5) y petición cortés. Be able to: habilidad, y necesario en tiempos donde can no existe (will be able to, have been able to). Was able to = logró hacerlo en una ocasión concreta.
cards.example: I can drive. / She could read at age 4. / You'll be able to vote next year. / We were able to finish on time.
cards.audio: I can drive. / She could read at age 4. / You'll be able to vote next year. / We were able to finish on time.

cards.front: When I was a child, I {{could}} climb any tree. (habilidad pasada)
After the course, you {{will be able to}} build your own app. (habilidad futura)
8.7 · ¿Cómo se dan consejos con should, ought to y had better?
cards.back: Should y ought to: consejo o lo que es buena idea (You should sleep more). Had better ('d better) + verbo base: advertencia fuerte, hay consecuencia negativa si no se hace (You'd better hurry or you'll miss the bus). Negativo: shouldn't, had better not.
cards.example: You should recycle. / He ought to apologize. / We'd better leave now. / You'd better not be late.
cards.audio: You should recycle. / He ought to apologize. / We'd better leave now. / You'd better not be late.

cards.front: It's getting dark. We {{'d better|had better}} go home now. (advertencia)
You'd better {{not}} forget her birthday. (negativo de had better)
8.8 · ¿Qué significan los negativos de los modales?
cards.back: Must not / mustn't = prohibido. Don't have to = no es necesario. Shouldn't = no es buena idea. Can't = no puede / no se permite / es imposible. May not / might not = quizá no. Had better not = más vale que no.
cards.example: You mustn't touch that; it's dangerous. / You don't have to come; it's optional. / You shouldn't eat so much sugar.
cards.audio: You mustn't touch that; it's dangerous. / You don't have to come; it's optional. / You shouldn't eat so much sugar.

cards.front: You {{don't have to}} pay; it's free. (no es necesario)
cards.back: don't have to = no hace falta.

cards.front: You {{mustn't|must not}} use your phone while driving. (prohibido)
She {{might not}} come to the party; she's busy. (quizá no)
8.9 · ¿Cómo se usa must para conclusiones o deducciones?
cards.back: Must + verbo base expresa una conclusión lógica casi segura sobre el presente: She isn't answering. She must be busy. Negativo: must not (no lleva contracción en este uso): He must not know the answer. Con estados continuos: must be + -ing.
cards.example: You've worked all day. You must be tired. / The lights are off. They must not be home. / He must be sleeping.
cards.audio: You've worked all day. You must be tired. / The lights are off. They must not be home. / He must be sleeping.

cards.front: He has three houses. He {{must}} be rich. (deducción)
She didn't eat anything. She {{must not}} be hungry. (deducción negativa)
8.10 · ¿Cómo se expresa posibilidad con may y might?
cards.back: May y might (+ verbo base) indican que algo es posible pero no seguro (quizá, tal vez), en presente o futuro: It may rain. She might be at home. Might es un poco menos seguro. Con -ing: He may be working. No se usan en preguntas para posibilidad; se dice 'Do you think…?'.
cards.example: I might go to the gym later. / They may not agree. / It might be true.
cards.audio: I might go to the gym later. / They may not agree. / It might be true.

cards.front: Take an umbrella. It {{might|may}} rain later. (quizá)
I don't know where he is. He {{may be}} at the library. (may + be)
8.11 · ¿Cómo se usan los modales para ser cortés?
cards.back: Peticiones: Can/Could/Would you + verbo (Could you help me?). Pedir permiso: Can/Could/May I…? (May I sit here?). Ofrecer: Would you like…? Can I get you…? Preferencia: I would rather ('d rather) + base. Deseo cortés: I would like ('d like) + sustantivo/to + verbo. 'Would you mind + -ing?' también es muy cortés.
cards.example: Could you pass the salt? / May I borrow your pen? / Would you like some coffee? / I'd like a window seat. / I'd rather stay home.
cards.audio: Could you pass the salt? / May I borrow your pen? / Would you like some coffee? / I'd like a window seat. / I'd rather stay home.

cards.front: {{Could}} you help me with this box, please? (petición cortés)
{{May}} I leave early today? (pedir permiso, formal)
I {{'d like|would like}} a cup of coffee, please. (deseo cortés)
I'd {{rather}} walk than take a taxi. (preferencia)

decks.name: U9 · Presente perfecto y presente perfecto continuo
decks.description: Unidad 9 (Virtual Communities): formas del presente perfecto, participio pasado, adverbios (already, yet, just, ever, never), usos (continuación, repetición, tiempo indefinido), contraste con el pasado simple y el presente perfecto continuo.

cards.back: Have/has + participio pasado. Has con he/she/it; have con el resto. Contracciones: I've, you've, he's, she's, we've, they've. Negativo: haven't/hasn't. Preguntas: Have you…? Has she…? Respuestas cortas: Yes, I have. / No, she hasn't.
cards.example: I have finished my homework. / She has lived here since 2020. / Have you eaten? / They haven't arrived yet.
cards.audio: I have finished my homework. / She has lived here since 2020. / Have you eaten? / They haven't arrived yet.

cards.front: We {{have}} worked here for two years. (have/has)

cards.back: Regulares: igual que el pasado, -ed (worked/worked). Irregulares: a veces igual al pasado (buy/bought/bought, have/had/had), a veces distinto (go/went/gone, see/saw/seen, write/wrote/written, eat/ate/eaten, take/took/taken, do/did/done, be/was/been, know/knew/known, give/gave/given, speak/spoke/spoken).
cards.example: I have seen that movie. / She has written three books. / They have gone home. / He has done a great job.
cards.audio: I have seen that movie. / She has written three books. / They have gone home. / He has done a great job.

cards.front: She has {{written}} two apps this year. (write)
9.3 · ¿Cómo se usan los adverbios con el presente perfecto (already, yet, just, ever, never, still)?
cards.back: Already (ya, afirmativo; entre have y el participio o al final). Yet (todavía/ya, en negativas y preguntas, al final). Just (acabar de; entre have y participio). Ever (alguna vez, en preguntas). Never (nunca; entre have y participio). Still + negativo (todavía no): I still haven't finished.
cards.example: I've already eaten. / Has she called yet? / They've just left. / Have you ever tried sushi? / He has never flown.
cards.audio: I've already eaten. / Has she called yet? / They've just left. / Have you ever tried sushi? / He has never flown.

cards.front: I have {{already}} finished the report. (ya, afirmativo)
Has the package arrived {{yet}}? (ya, en pregunta)
She has {{just}} left the office. (acaba de)
9.4 · ¿Cuáles son los usos principales del presente perfecto?
cards.back: 1) Acción o estado que empezó en el pasado y continúa hasta ahora (for/since). 2) Repetición de una acción hasta ahora (three times, many times, so far). 3) Acción en un momento indefinido del pasado con importancia ahora (ever, never, already, yet, just, recently). Nunca con un tiempo pasado concreto (yesterday, in 2010 → pasado simple).
cards.example: I have lived here for 10 years. / She has called three times today. / Have you ever been to Peru? / I've just had lunch.
cards.audio: I have lived here for 10 years. / She has called three times today. / Have you ever been to Peru? / I've just had lunch.

cards.front: I {{have known}} him since we were kids. (know; continúa)
She {{has seen}} that movie four times. (see; repetición)
9.5 · ¿Cómo se usa el presente perfecto con for y since (continuación hasta el presente)?
cards.back: For + duración (for two hours, for ten years); since + punto de inicio (since 2015, since Monday, since I was a child). Suele ir con estados o situaciones que siguen: I have been a student at UVG for three years. Pregunta: How long have you…?
cards.example: We have been friends since 2018. / He has worked at BYTE for two years. / How long have you had that car?
cards.audio: We have been friends since 2018. / He has worked at BYTE for two years. / How long have you had that car?

cards.front: I have lived in Ciudad Vieja {{for}} ten years. (duración)
She has worked here {{since}} January. (punto de inicio)
How {{long}} have you studied English? — For six years.
9.6 · ¿Cuándo se usa pasado simple, presente perfecto y presente simple para hablar de duración?
cards.back: Presente perfecto: empezó en el pasado y sigue (I have lived here for 5 years — sigo aquí). Pasado simple: terminó (I lived there for 5 years — ya no). Presente simple: estado actual sin decir desde cuándo (I live here). Con for, elige según si la situación continúa o no.
cards.example: She has taught at UVG for 20 years. (sigue) / She taught at UVG for 20 years. (se jubiló) / She teaches at UVG.
cards.audio: She has taught at UVG for 20 years. (sigue) / She taught at UVG for 20 years. (se jubiló) / She teaches at UVG.

cards.front: My grandfather {{worked}} at the factory for 30 years. Now he's retired. (work)
I {{have worked}} at BYTE since 2023. I love my job. (work; sigo ahí)
9.7 · ¿Cómo se usa el presente perfecto para repetición del pasado al presente?
cards.back: Con expresiones de cantidad de veces hasta ahora: once, twice, three times, many times, several times, so far, up to now, in the last/past week. La acción puede repetirse aún. Pregunta: How many times have you…?
cards.example: I have been to the doctor twice this month. / She has changed jobs three times. / We've had five meetings so far.
cards.audio: I have been to the doctor twice this month. / She has changed jobs three times. / We've had five meetings so far.

cards.front: How many {{times}} have you seen this movie? — Three times.
It {{has rained}} a lot this week. (rain; la semana sigue)
9.8 · ¿Cómo se usa el presente perfecto para un tiempo indefinido en el pasado?
cards.back: Cuando no importa o no se dice cuándo, sino el resultado o la experiencia: I have lost my keys (no las tengo). Con ever/never (experiencia), already/yet/just, recently/lately. Si se especifica el momento, cambia a pasado simple: I lost my keys yesterday.
cards.example: Have you ever tried tamales? / I've already seen it. / She has recently moved. / He hasn't called yet.
cards.audio: Have you ever tried tamales? / I've already seen it. / She has recently moved. / He hasn't called yet.

cards.front: I {{have lost}} my wallet. Can you help me look for it? (lose; resultado ahora)
9.9 · ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre el presente perfecto y el pasado simple?
cards.back: Pasado simple: momento concreto y terminado (yesterday, last year, in 2020, ago, when I was…). Presente perfecto: tiempo no especificado, conexión con el presente, o periodo que no ha terminado (today, this week, so far). Tras una pregunta general en presente perfecto, los detalles van en pasado simple: Have you seen it? Yes, I saw it last week.
cards.example: I have visited Mexico. / I visited Mexico in 2019. / She has called twice today. / She called twice yesterday.
cards.audio: I have visited Mexico. / I visited Mexico in 2019. / She has called twice today. / She called twice yesterday.

cards.front: I {{have seen}} that movie, but I don't remember when. (see)
Have you eaten? — Yes, I {{ate}} an hour ago. (eat)
9.10 · ¿Cómo se forma el presente perfecto continuo?
cards.back: Have/has + been + verbo-ing. Contracciones: I've been working, she's been studying. Negativo: haven't/hasn't been + -ing. Pregunta: How long have you been waiting?
cards.example: I have been studying for two hours. / She has been working here since May. / Have you been sleeping well?
cards.audio: I have been studying for two hours. / She has been working here since May. / Have you been sleeping well?

cards.front: It {{has been raining}} since this morning. (rain)
We {{have been waiting}} for an hour! (wait)
9.11 · ¿Cuándo se usa el presente perfecto continuo?
cards.back: Para una acción que empezó en el pasado y continúa ahora, destacando la duración o que es continua (I've been reading all day). Con for/since y how long. Con verbos de estado (know, have, be, like) no se usa el continuo → presente perfecto simple: I have known her for years. Con verbos como live/work/study ambos son posibles.
cards.example: She has been learning English for three years. / I've been thinking about your idea. / How long have you been living here? / I have had this phone since 2022.
cards.audio: She has been learning English for three years. / I've been thinking about your idea. / How long have you been living here? / I have had this phone since 2022.

cards.front: I {{have been studying}} Kotlin since March. (study; énfasis en actividad continua)
I {{have had}} this laptop for five years. (have = poseer; estado)

decks.name: U10 · Gerundios e infinitivos
decks.description: Unidad 10 (Jobs): gerundios como sujeto y objeto, preposición + gerundio, infinitivos tras it, adjetivos y verbos, objeto + infinitivo, infinitivo de propósito, verbos que aceptan ambos.

cards.back: Es la forma verbo-ing usada como sustantivo: puede ser sujeto (Swimming is fun), objeto de un verbo (I enjoy swimming) u objeto de una preposición (I'm good at swimming). Negativo: not + -ing (not knowing). No confundir con el presente continuo, que lleva be.
cards.example: Reading helps you learn. / She avoids driving at night. / Thanks for coming.
cards.audio: Reading helps you learn. / She avoids driving at night. / Thanks for coming.

cards.front: {{Running}} every morning keeps me healthy. (run; sujeto)
I enjoy {{cooking}} for my friends. (cook; objeto)
10.2 · ¿Cómo se usan los gerundios como sujeto?
cards.back: El gerundio (o la frase con gerundio) funciona como sujeto singular y lleva verbo en singular: Learning languages takes time. Se puede reformular con it + infinitivo: It takes time to learn languages.
cards.example: Working from home has advantages. / Eating vegetables is good for you. / Finding a job isn't easy.
cards.audio: Working from home has advantages. / Eating vegetables is good for you. / Finding a job isn't easy.

cards.front: Finding a good job {{takes}} time. (take; concordancia)

cards.back: Después de: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, keep (on), quit, stop, suggest, recommend, consider, practice, miss, admit, deny, delay, postpone, put off, imagine, appreciate, can't help, dislike, discuss, risk. Ejemplo: She finished writing the report. Hay un mazo de apéndice con la lista completa.
cards.example: I finished reading the book. / Do you mind waiting? / He keeps calling me. / We should consider moving.
cards.audio: I finished reading the book. / Do you mind waiting? / He keeps calling me. / We should consider moving.

cards.front: She finished {{writing}} the report at midnight. (write)
10.4 · ¿Qué forma verbal va después de una preposición?
cards.back: Después de una preposición (in, on, at, of, for, about, without, before, after, by, to en algunos casos) siempre va gerundio: interested in learning, good at coding, thank you for helping, without saying, before leaving, look forward to seeing you, used to (acostumbrado a) + -ing. Ojo: 'to' de infinitivo NO es preposición (want to go).
cards.example: I'm interested in working abroad. / She's good at solving problems. / He left without saying goodbye. / I look forward to meeting you.
cards.audio: I'm interested in working abroad. / She's good at solving problems. / He left without saying goodbye. / I look forward to meeting you.

cards.front: 10.5 · ¿Qué es un infinitivo y cómo se usa?
cards.back: To + verbo base (to work, to be). Va tras ciertos verbos (want to go), tras adjetivos (happy to help), tras it + adjetivo (It's important to sleep), tras objetos (I want you to come) y para expresar propósito (I study to learn). Negativo: not to + verbo (I decided not to go).
cards.example: I want to travel. / It's easy to learn. / She told me to wait. / He came here to study. / Try not to worry.
cards.audio: I want to travel. / It's easy to learn. / She told me to wait. / He came here to study. / Try not to worry.

cards.front: I decided {{not to go}} to the party. (negativo del infinitivo)
She hopes {{to find}} a better job. (find)
10.6 · ¿Cómo se usa el infinitivo después de expresiones con it?
cards.back: It + be + adjetivo + (for + persona) + to + verbo: It's important to sleep well. It's hard for me to wake up early. También it + takes/costs: It takes time to learn. Equivale a usar el gerundio como sujeto.
cards.example: It's difficult to find parking here. / It's necessary for students to register. / It takes two hours to get there.
cards.audio: It's difficult to find parking here. / It's necessary for students to register. / It takes two hours to get there.

cards.front: It's important {{to learn}} from your mistakes. (learn)
It's hard {{for}} me to concentrate with noise. (persona)
It {{takes}} 45 minutes to get to the university. (take)

cards.back: Muchos adjetivos de emoción o evaluación: happy, glad, sad, sorry, afraid, ready, prepared, willing, eager, proud, lucky, surprised, easy, hard, difficult, important, necessary, impossible. Ejemplo: I'm happy to help. She was surprised to see me.
cards.example: I'm glad to hear that. / He's ready to start. / We were lucky to get tickets. / It's impossible to know.
cards.audio: I'm glad to hear that. / He's ready to start. / We were lucky to get tickets. / It's impossible to know.

cards.front: I'm sorry {{to hear}} about your accident. (hear)

cards.back: want, need, would like, hope, plan, decide, expect, promise, agree, refuse, learn, try, forget, seem, manage, offer, prepare, pretend, intend, afford, deserve, tend, attempt. Ejemplo: I plan to study abroad. Hay un mazo de apéndice con la lista completa.
cards.example: We decided to leave early. / She promised to call. / I can't afford to buy a car. / He refused to answer.
cards.audio: We decided to leave early. / She promised to call. / I can't afford to buy a car. / He refused to answer.

cards.front: I plan {{to visit}} my cousins in December. (visit)
We can't afford {{to travel}} this year. (travel)
10.9 · ¿Cómo se usa un objeto antes del infinitivo?
cards.back: Verbo + objeto (persona) + to + verbo: want, would like, expect, ask, tell, advise, allow, permit, encourage, remind, invite, teach, need, help. Ejemplo: I want you to listen. She told me to wait. Con help el 'to' es opcional: help me (to) study. Con make y let NO se usa to: make me laugh, let me go.
cards.example: My boss expects me to work late. / They invited us to join. / Let me help you. / The joke made everyone laugh.
cards.audio: My boss expects me to work late. / They invited us to join. / Let me help you. / The joke made everyone laugh.

cards.front: My mother wants {{me to}} study medicine. (objeto + to)
The teacher told us {{to read}} chapter 3. (read)
My parents let me {{stay}} out late. (stay; tras let)
That movie made me {{cry}}. (cry; tras make)
10.10 · ¿Cómo se expresa propósito con el infinitivo?
cards.back: To + verbo (o in order to + verbo, más formal) responde a '¿para qué?': I went to the store to buy milk. No se usa 'for + verbo' para propósito con verbos ('for buying' ✗); for + sustantivo sí: I went for milk.
cards.example: She's saving money to buy a car. / He exercises in order to stay healthy. / I called to say thanks.
cards.audio: She's saving money to buy a car. / He exercises in order to stay healthy. / I called to say thanks.

cards.front: I went to the bank {{to open}} an account. (open; propósito)
We use this app {{to}} track our study time. (para)
10.11 · ¿Qué verbos aceptan gerundio o infinitivo, y cuándo cambia el significado?
cards.back: Sin cambio de sentido: begin, start, continue, like, love, hate, prefer, can't stand. Con cambio: stop + -ing (dejar de hacer) vs. stop + to (parar para hacer); remember + -ing (recordar haber hecho) vs. remember + to (acordarse de hacer); forget + -ing / forget + to (igual lógica); try + -ing (probar a) vs. try + to (intentar, esforzarse).
cards.example: I like reading / to read. / He stopped smoking. / He stopped to smoke. / Remember to lock the door. / I remember locking it.
cards.audio: I like reading / to read. / He stopped smoking. / He stopped to smoke. / Remember to lock the door. / I remember locking it.

cards.front: Remember {{to lock}} the door when you leave. (lock; acuérdate de hacerlo)
cards.back: remember to + verbo = acordarse de hacer.

cards.front: I remember {{locking}} the door; I'm sure. (lock; recuerdo haberlo hecho)
She stopped {{drinking}} coffee last year. (drink; dejó de)
We stopped {{to buy}} gas on the way. (buy; paramos para)

decks.name: U11 · Cláusulas de adjetivo (relativas)
decks.description: Unidad 11 (Making Connections): pronombres relativos como sujeto y como objeto, objeto de preposición, whose + sustantivo, where y when.

cards.back: Es una cláusula que describe a un sustantivo y va justo después de él. Empieza con un pronombre relativo: who (personas), which (cosas), that (personas o cosas), whose (posesión), where (lugares), when (tiempos). Ejemplo: The app that I built is free.
cards.example: I have a friend who lives in Canada. / This is the book which changed my life. / The house where I grew up is small.
cards.audio: I have a friend who lives in Canada. / This is the book which changed my life. / The house where I grew up is small.

cards.front: The woman {{who|that}} teaches this class is from Peru. (persona, sujeto)
I love the app {{that|which}} you recommended. (cosa)
11.2 · ¿Cómo se usan los pronombres relativos como sujeto de la cláusula?
cards.back: Cuando el relativo es el sujeto de la cláusula, va seguido directamente del verbo: people who speak English; a phone that costs $100. El pronombre NO puede omitirse. El verbo concuerda con el sustantivo descrito: a student who works / students who work.
cards.example: I know a man who fixes phones. / We need a car that doesn't use much gas. / She has friends who live abroad.
cards.audio: I know a man who fixes phones. / We need a car that doesn't use much gas. / She has friends who live abroad.

cards.front: I have a cousin who {{lives}} in Spain. (live; concordancia con cousin)
Programmers {{who}} know Kotlin are in demand. (personas, sujeto)
11.3 · ¿Cómo se usan los pronombres relativos como objeto de la cláusula?
cards.back: Cuando el relativo es el objeto de la cláusula, después viene sujeto + verbo: the book (that/which) I read; the person (who/whom/that) I met. En este caso el pronombre puede omitirse: the book I read. No se repite el objeto: 'the book that I read it' ✗.
cards.example: The movie (that) we saw was great. / The people (who) you met are my coworkers. / Is this the phone (that) you want?
cards.audio: The movie (that) we saw was great. / The people (who) you met are my coworkers. / Is this the phone (that) you want?

cards.front: The pizza {{that|which}} we ordered was cold. (cosa, objeto; también puede omitirse)
cards.back: Se puede omitir: The pizza we ordered.

cards.front: The teacher I like most {{is}} Mr. Lemus. (be; relativo omitido)
11.4 · ¿Cómo se usan los relativos como objeto de una preposición?
cards.back: Informal: la preposición va al final de la cláusula y el relativo puede omitirse: the friend (who/that) I live with; the company (that) she works for. Formal: preposición + whom/which al inicio: the friend with whom I live; the company for which she works.
cards.example: The neighbor (that) I talked to is nice. / The project (which) I'm working on is hard. / The man to whom I spoke was the manager. (formal)
cards.audio: The neighbor (that) I talked to is nice. / The project (which) I'm working on is hard. / The man to whom I spoke was the manager. (formal)

cards.front: The person I talked {{to}} was very helpful. (preposición al final)
That's the company {{for}} which she works. (formal: preposición + which)
11.5 · ¿Cómo se usa whose + sustantivo en una cláusula relativa?
cards.back: Whose indica posesión y va siempre seguido de un sustantivo; sustituye a his/her/their/its: I have a friend whose brother is a pilot (= his brother). Sirve para personas y cosas; nunca se omite.
cards.example: She's the student whose project won. / We stayed at a hotel whose rooms were huge. / That's the man whose car was stolen.
cards.audio: She's the student whose project won. / We stayed at a hotel whose rooms were huge. / That's the man whose car was stolen.

cards.front: I have a coworker {{whose}} wife is a doctor. (posesión)
The author {{whose}} book we read is coming to UVG. (posesión)
11.6 · ¿Cómo se usan where y when en cláusulas relativas?
cards.back: Where sustituye a 'in/at that place': the city where I was born (= in which). When sustituye a 'at that time': the day when we met (= on which). Con when el pronombre puede omitirse: the day we met. No se añade preposición después: 'the city where I live in' ✗.
cards.example: This is the café where we had our first date. / I'll never forget the day when I graduated. / Do you remember the year (when) we moved?
cards.audio: This is the café where we had our first date. / I'll never forget the day when I graduated. / Do you remember the year (when) we moved?

cards.front: This is the neighborhood {{where}} I grew up. (lugar)
I remember the day {{when}} you were born. (tiempo)

decks.name: U12 · Superlativos y comparativos
decks.description: Unidad 12 (Sports and Athletes): formas y uso del superlativo y del comparativo, as…as, as many/much…as, the same…as, like y alike.

cards.front: 12.1 · ¿Cómo se forma el superlativo de adjetivos y adverbios?
cards.back: Una sílaba: the + -est (the tallest, the fastest). Terminados en -e: + -st (the largest). Consonante-vocal-consonante: duplica (the biggest, the hottest). Dos sílabas en -y: -iest (the happiest, the easiest). Dos o más sílabas: the most + adjetivo (the most beautiful, the most quickly). Irregulares: good → the best, bad → the worst, far → the farthest/furthest, little → the least, much/many → the most.
cards.example: the highest mountain / the most expensive car / the best player / the worst day
cards.audio: the highest mountain / the most expensive car / the best player / the worst day

cards.front: Tajumulco is the {{highest}} volcano in Central America. (high)
That was the {{most interesting}} class of the semester. (interesting)
She is the {{best}} player on the team. (good)
Today was the {{hottest}} day of the year. (hot)
12.2 · ¿Cuándo y cómo se usa el superlativo?
cards.back: Compara una cosa con todo un grupo (tres o más). Va con the y a menudo con in + lugar/grupo (the tallest in the class), of + grupo (the best of all) o con presente perfecto + ever (the best movie I have ever seen). 'One of the' + superlativo + plural: one of the best restaurants.
cards.example: She is the youngest in her family. / It's the most popular sport in the world. / This is the best pizza I've ever eaten.
cards.audio: She is the youngest in her family. / It's the most popular sport in the world. / This is the best pizza I've ever eaten.

cards.front: He is the smartest student {{in}} the class. (preposición)
That's the best coffee I have {{ever}} tasted. (presente perfecto + ever)
Antigua is one of the most beautiful {{cities}} in Guatemala. (city; tras 'one of')

cards.back: Una sílaba: -er + than (taller than, faster than). -e: + -r (larger). CVC duplica (bigger). Dos sílabas en -y: -ier (happier, easier). Dos o más sílabas: more + adjetivo (more expensive, more carefully). Irregulares: good → better, bad → worse, far → farther/further, little → less, much/many → more. Menos: less + adjetivo.
cards.example: taller than / more expensive than / better than / less interesting than
cards.audio: taller than / more expensive than / better than / less interesting than

cards.front: This phone is {{more expensive}} than that one. (expensive)
The exam was {{easier}} than I expected. (easy)

cards.back: Compara dos cosas o personas con than: A is bigger than B. Se puede omitir than si está claro: This one is cheaper. Intensificadores: much/a lot/far + comparativo (much better), a little/slightly (a little faster). Tras than se usa pronombre de objeto en habla informal (than me) o sujeto + verbo (than I am). Doble comparativo: The more you practice, the better you get.
cards.example: Soccer is more popular than baseball here. / She runs much faster than me. / The sooner, the better.
cards.audio: Soccer is more popular than baseball here. / She runs much faster than me. / The sooner, the better.

cards.front: This laptop is {{much}} faster than my old one. (intensificador: mucho)
The {{more}} you practice, the better you get. (doble comparativo)

cards.back: As + adjetivo/adverbio + as indica igualdad: She is as tall as her mother. En negativo, not as … as = menos que: This car isn't as fast as that one. Con pronombres: as tall as me / as tall as I am. Expresiones: as soon as possible, as much as you can.
cards.example: He is as smart as his brother. / I don't sing as well as you. / Come as soon as you can.
cards.audio: He is as smart as his brother. / I don't sing as well as you. / Come as soon as you can.

cards.front: My sister is as tall {{as}} me. (igualdad)
This movie is {{not as}} good as the book. (menos que, con as)
12.6 · ¿Cómo se usa as many / as much … as?
cards.back: Con sustantivos: as many + contable plural + as (as many friends as); as much + incontable + as (as much money as). También con verbos: I work as much as you. Negativo: not as many/much … as = menos.
cards.example: I have as many books as my teacher. / She doesn't earn as much money as he does. / Eat as much as you want.
cards.audio: I have as many books as my teacher. / She doesn't earn as much money as he does. / Eat as much as you want.

cards.front: I don't have as {{many}} classes as you this semester. (contable)
He drinks as {{much}} coffee as I do. (incontable)

cards.back: The same + sustantivo + as: We have the same teacher as last year. Sin sustantivo: My car is the same as yours. Lo contrario: different from. También con sujeto plural: We are the same age. She and I have the same birthday.
cards.example: He wears the same size as me. / Your phone is the same as mine. / They go to the same school.
cards.audio: He wears the same size as me. / Your phone is the same as mine. / They go to the same school.

cards.front: She is the same {{age}} as my brother. (sustantivo: edad)
