My schedule is the same {{as}} yours. (igual que)
My schedule is different {{from}} yours. (distinto de)
12.8 · ¿Cómo se muestra similitud con like y alike?
cards.back: Like + sustantivo/pronombre: She looks like her mother; He acts like a child. Alike va al final, con sujeto plural: They look alike; The twins are alike. También be alike/be like: My brother and I are alike. Like se usa con verbos como look, sound, feel, taste, smell, act, be.
cards.example: This tastes like chicken. / You and your dad are alike. / He sings like a professional.
cards.audio: This tastes like chicken. / You and your dad are alike. / He sings like a professional.

cards.front: The two sisters look {{alike}}. (like/alike; al final)

decks.name: U13 · Voz activa y pasiva
decks.description: Unidad 13 (The Law): forma y uso de la voz pasiva, negativos y preguntas, verbos transitivos e intransitivos.

cards.front: 13.1 · ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre voz activa y voz pasiva?
cards.back: Activa: el sujeto hace la acción (The judge made the decision). Pasiva: el sujeto recibe la acción (The decision was made by the judge). El objeto de la activa pasa a ser sujeto de la pasiva; el agente se menciona con by solo si es importante.
cards.example: Someone stole my bike. → My bike was stolen. / They speak Spanish here. → Spanish is spoken here.
cards.audio: Someone stole my bike. → My bike was stolen. / They speak Spanish here. → Spanish is spoken here.

cards.front: Active: They built the bridge in 1990. Passive: The bridge {{was built}} in 1990. (build)
The email was sent {{by}} the manager. (agente)

cards.back: Be (en el tiempo que corresponda) + participio pasado. Presente: is/are made. Pasado: was/were made. Futuro: will be made. Presente perfecto: has/have been made. Con modales: can be made, must be made. Presente continuo: is being made.
cards.example: The office is cleaned every day. / The law was passed last year. / The results will be announced tomorrow. / The car has been repaired.
cards.audio: The office is cleaned every day. / The law was passed last year. / The results will be announced tomorrow. / The car has been repaired.

cards.front: Cars {{are made}} in many countries. (make; presente)
The winner {{will be announced}} on Friday. (announce; futuro)
The house {{has been sold}}. (sell; presente perfecto)
This form must {{be signed}} by a parent. (sign; con modal)

cards.back: Cuando no se sabe quién hizo la acción (My phone was stolen), cuando no importa o es obvio (The suspect was arrested), cuando lo importante es la acción o el receptor, o en textos formales, científicos y de leyes. Se usa by + agente solo si aporta información.
cards.example: English is spoken in many countries. / The letter was delivered this morning. / The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.
cards.audio: English is spoken in many countries. / The letter was delivered this morning. / The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.

cards.front: My wallet {{was stolen}} on the bus. (steal; no se sabe quién)
Spanish {{is spoken}} in Guatemala. (speak; agente obvio)
13.4 · ¿Cómo se forman los negativos y las preguntas en voz pasiva?
cards.back: Negativo: be + not + participio (isn't made, wasn't sent, won't be finished, hasn't been done). Preguntas: Be + sujeto + participio (Was the letter sent? When was it sent? Has the work been done?). Con modales: Can it be fixed?
cards.example: The bill wasn't paid. / Is the museum closed on Mondays? / When was the phone invented? / Has the package been delivered?
cards.audio: The bill wasn't paid. / Is the museum closed on Mondays? / When was the phone invented? / Has the package been delivered?

cards.front: The report {{wasn't|was not}} finished on time. (finish; negativo pasado)
{{Was}} the phone invented by Bell? (invent; pregunta)
13.5 · ¿Qué son los verbos transitivos e intransitivos y por qué importan para la pasiva?
cards.back: Transitivos: llevan objeto directo (build a house, write a letter) y pueden pasar a pasiva. Intransitivos: no llevan objeto (happen, arrive, sleep, die, go, come, fall, live, seem) y NO tienen pasiva: 'The accident was happened' ✗. Algunos verbos son ambos según el uso.
cards.example: The accident happened at 5. (no pasiva) / She arrived late. / The house was built in 1950. / He died in 2001.
cards.audio: The accident happened at 5. (no pasiva) / She arrived late. / The house was built in 1950. / He died in 2001.

cards.front: The accident {{happened}} last night. (happen; sin pasiva)
The book {{was written}} in 1998. (write; transitivo, pasiva)

decks.name: U14 · Artículos, other/another y pronombres indefinidos
decks.description: Unidad 14 (Money): panorama de los artículos, generalizaciones, clasificar/definir, sustantivos específicos y no específicos, cantidad, other/another, pronombres definidos e indefinidos.

cards.front: 14.1 · ¿Cuáles son los artículos y cuándo se usa cada uno?
cards.back: A/an (indefinido): contable singular no específico (a job, an apple; 'an' ante sonido vocálico: an hour, a university). The (definido): algo específico o ya mencionado, único (the sun), superlativos, o conocido por ambos. Sin artículo (Ø): plurales e incontables en general (Money is important; I like dogs).
cards.example: I need a job. / The job I found is great. / An hour ago. / Water is essential.
cards.audio: I need a job. / The job I found is great. / An hour ago. / Water is essential.

cards.front: I have {{an}} interview at {{a}} university tomorrow. (a/an)

cards.back: Para generalizar: plural sin artículo (Cats are independent), incontable sin artículo (Music relaxes me), o a/an + singular (A cat is an independent animal). No se usa the para generalizar: 'The cats are independent' habla de gatos concretos.
cards.example: Children need love. / Coffee keeps me awake. / A smartphone is a small computer.
cards.audio: Children need love. / Coffee keeps me awake. / A smartphone is a small computer.

cards.front: {{Ø|-|x|nada|sin artículo}} Dogs are loyal animals. (artículo: a / the / Ø)
cards.hint: plural general → sin artículo; escribe - si no hay artículo

cards.front: {{Ø|-|x|nada|sin artículo}} Money can't buy happiness. (artículo: a / the / Ø)
cards.hint: incontable general; escribe - si no hay

cards.front: 14.3 · ¿Cómo se clasifica o define el sujeto con artículos?
cards.back: Para decir qué es algo o alguien (clasificar/definir) se usa a/an con singular contable: She is a doctor. A tamale is a traditional food. Con plural, sin artículo: They are doctors. Con incontable, sin artículo: Rice is a grain (rice sin artículo, grain con a).
cards.example: My father is an engineer. / An app is a program for phones. / Antigua is a colonial city.
cards.audio: My father is an engineer. / An app is a program for phones. / Antigua is a colonial city.

cards.front: They are {{Ø|-|x|nada|sin artículo}} teachers. (artículo: a / the / Ø)
14.4 · ¿Cómo se usan los artículos con sustantivos no específicos?
cards.back: Un sustantivo no específico (uno cualquiera, no uno concreto) lleva a/an en singular contable (I want a sandwich), some/any o Ø en plural e incontable (I bought some apples; Do you have any milk?; I need help). Es la primera vez que se menciona algo.
cards.example: I need a pen. / There are some emails for you. / She bought Ø bread and Ø cheese.
cards.audio: I need a pen. / There are some emails for you. / She bought Ø bread and Ø cheese.

cards.front: I need {{some}} information about the course. (incontable, no específico, afirmativa)
14.5 · ¿Cómo se usa the con sustantivos específicos?
cards.back: The va con cosas específicas: ya mencionadas (I bought a car. The car is red), definidas por el contexto o una frase (the book on the table, the president of Guatemala), únicas (the moon, the Internet), conocidas por ambos (the kitchen), superlativos y ordinales (the best, the first), y ciertos nombres geográficos (the United States, the Pacific, the Andes).
cards.example: Close the door. / The teacher we had last year was great. / Where's the bathroom? / She lives in the U.S.
cards.audio: Close the door. / The teacher we had last year was great. / Where's the bathroom? / She lives in the U.S.

cards.front: I saw a movie last night. {{The}} movie was about a robot. (segunda mención)
Can you pass me {{the}} salt? (contexto compartido)
She is {{the}} tallest girl in the class. (superlativo)
14.6 · ¿Cómo se usan los artículos con palabras de cantidad?
cards.back: Cantidad no específica: some/any/a lot of/many/much/a few/a little + sustantivo (some students, a lot of money). Cantidad específica (parte de un grupo conocido): some/many/most/all/none/one + OF + the/my/these + sustantivo (some of the students, most of my friends, all of the money). Most + plural = en general (Most people); most of the + plural = específico.
cards.example: Most students work hard. / Most of the students in my class work. / Some of the money is missing. / All of my cousins live here.
cards.audio: Most students work hard. / Most of the students in my class work. / Some of the money is missing. / All of my cousins live here.

cards.front: Most {{of the}} students in this class are from Sacatepéquez. (grupo específico)
Some {{of}} my friends speak English. (parte de un grupo)

cards.back: Another = an + other: otro más, uno adicional o distinto, con singular contable (another cup, another day). Other + plural/incontable no específico: other people, other information. The other + singular = el otro (el último que queda); the other + plural = los otros/demás. Others (pronombre, plural): Some like tea; others like coffee. The others = los demás (específicos).
cards.example: Can I have another cookie? / Some students study at night; others study in the morning. / I have two cats: one is black, the other is white.
cards.audio: Can I have another cookie? / Some students study at night; others study in the morning. / I have two cats: one is black, the other is white.

cards.front: This coffee is great. Can I have {{another}} cup?
I have two brothers. One lives here and {{the other}} lives in Spain. (el otro, el último)
Some people love the city; {{others}} prefer the countryside. (otros, pronombre)
14.8 · ¿Qué más hay que saber sobre other y another?
cards.back: Another puede ir con periodos y cantidades en plural si se ven como unidad: another two weeks, another ten dollars. Each other / one another = el uno al otro (mutuo). Every other day = un día sí y otro no. The other day = hace unos días. Other no lleva -s cuando va delante de un sustantivo ('others people' ✗).
cards.example: We need another three chairs. / They help each other. / I go to the gym every other day. / I saw Ana the other day.
cards.audio: We need another three chairs. / They help each other. / I go to the gym every other day. / I saw Ana the other day.

cards.front: My sister and I call {{each other}} every day. (mutuamente)
I work out every {{other}} day. (un día sí, otro no)
There are {{other}} options we should consider. (other/others antes de sustantivo)
14.9 · ¿Cómo se usan los pronombres definidos e indefinidos (one, ones, it, them)?
cards.back: Para no repetir un sustantivo: one sustituye a a/an + singular no específico (I need a pen. Do you have one?); ones al plural (the red ones); it sustituye a un singular específico (I bought the book. I read it in a day); them al plural específico. Compuestos indefinidos: someone/somebody, anyone, no one, everyone, something, anything, nothing, everything (verbo en singular).
cards.example: I lost my phone, so I bought a new one. / Which shoes? The black ones. / Someone is at the door. / Everyone likes her.
cards.audio: I lost my phone, so I bought a new one. / Which shoes? The black ones. / Someone is at the door. / Everyone likes her.

cards.front: I don't have a laptop. I need to buy {{one}}. (uno cualquiera)
I bought the laptop yesterday, and I love {{it}}. (esa específica)
Which jeans do you like? The blue {{ones}}. (plural)

cards.front: D · remember: ¿cambia el significado con gerundio o infinitivo?
cards.back: remember + -ing = recordar haber hecho algo; remember + to = acordarse de hacer algo.

cards.front: D · forget: ¿cambia el significado con gerundio o infinitivo?
cards.back: forget + -ing = olvidar haber hecho; forget + to = olvidar hacer (no lo hiciste).

cards.front: D · stop: ¿cambia el significado con gerundio o infinitivo?
cards.back: stop + -ing = dejar de hacer; stop + to = parar para hacer otra cosa.

cards.front: D · try: ¿cambia el significado con gerundio o infinitivo?
cards.back: try + -ing = probar a (experimentar); try + to = intentar, esforzarse.

cards.front: D · ¿Qué adjetivos van seguidos de infinitivo (to + verbo)?
cards.back: Adjetivos de emoción, evaluación y disposición: afraid, ashamed, careful, certain, challenging, delighted, determined, difficult, disappointed, eager, easy, embarrassed, excited, glad, good, happy, hard, important, impossible, likely, lucky, necessary, pleased, prepared, proud, ready, relieved, reluctant, rewarding, right, sad, shocked, sorry, stupid, surprised, upset, useful, willing, wrong. Ejemplo: I'm happy to help; It's hard to say; She was ready to go.
cards.example: I'm glad to see you. / It's impossible to finish today. / They were surprised to win.
cards.audio: I'm glad to see you. / It's impossible to finish today. / They were surprised to win.
